newsitem.title: INDIA: India's RBI announces cut in banks' CRR on Jan 4.
newsitem.headline: India's RBI announces cut in banks' CRR on Jan 4.

text.p: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) said on Thursday that a 50 basis point cut in banks' cash reserve ratio (CRR) to 10.5 percent would take effect on January 4, 1997.
The central bank said in a statement the CRR would be cut to 10 percent from 11 percent in two stages of 50 basis points.
"The reduction will be effected in two phases of 0.5 percentage point each from the fortnights beginning from January 4 and January 18, 1997 respectively," the RBI said.
Lendable resources of banks would be augmented by 42.75 billion rupees through the two cuts, it said.
The reductions follow the monetary policy statement on October 19 when the RBI governor announced a total cut in CRR of 200 basis points in four stages.
The first two cuts of 50 basis points each were effected on October 26 and November 9, 1996.
The RBI chief had then said the next two cuts, to take place in January, would be subject to prevailing monetary and price conditions.
The cuts in CRR were introduced to increase liquidity with banks and to bring down interest rates.
Following the first two cuts, several state-run banks reduced their prime lending rates between 50 and 100 basis points to 14.5-15.0 percent per annum.
